en: The Original Text of the Great Body Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes,
excerpted from the Middle Volume of the Mahākaruṇā-sūtra.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Vajrabodhi, Tripitaka Master of the Great Propagation of the Dharma,
who was posthumously granted the title of Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si by the Great Tang, in accordance with imperial decree:
Namaḥ samantāya | Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya | Namo ’ryāvalokiteśvarāya...
Rājamūrdhābhiṣiktāya mahābhiṣiktāya mahākāruṇikāya namo mahāsattvaparāvartāya mūrdhābhiṣiktāya mahābhiṣiktāya mahākāruṇikāya namaḥ bhagavate vipulavimānasupratiṣṭhitasaṃkhyeya.

Oṃ suryashata-sahasrārci-kara-prabhāva-vasita-mūrdhaye mahāmani-mukuṭa-kuṇḍala-dharine vagvati padmapāṇaye sarvalokapāśa-mocanāya vighnaghāta-nudaka-samaviśeṣṭha sarvasattva-pari... (Note: This is a transliteration of a Sanskrit mantra.
The provided source text contains numerous orthographic errors and non-standard characters; the above represents a corrected and standardised version of the intended Sanskrit.)

Namaḥ tadyathā | oṃ bhrūṃ bhru maṅgalakaraṇa-tamas-timiropaha-vināśana-karāya te 'bhiṣiñcāmi mukhāgralāśmagāsākhārukṣaka-sarvabhayanudgatipraśamanakarāya samyaksambuddha-samantabhadra | Namo tadyathā | Oṃ bhrūṃ bhru maṅgalakaraṇa-tamas-timiropaha-vināśana-karāya te abhiṣiñcāmi mukhāgralāśmagāsākhārukṣaka-sarvabhayanudgatipraśamanakarāya samyaksambuddha-samantabhadra.

Kara sarva-sattvānāṃ paritrāṇa-kara samasta-sattva-samāsivaśya-kara ihehi ehi maṅgala-mūrti-sattva-vārana-padma-rucāmbuda-maṅgala-rūpa-jāta-mukuṭa-ghṛṇi-śrī-maṇi-karṇaka-rājita-vāra-veṇi-nirjita-ghṛṇi.

Mulu muyu muyu mentsa mentsa ṛkṣa ṛkṣa mama [name] samāsattvānām ca samasaye bhiḥ dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna dhu ru dhu ru gāye gāye gadhaye gadhaye hasa hasa prahasa prahasa kare svāhā namaḥ [name] hola hola saṃhola saṃhola.
Hara dūruṭi dūruṭi maṃha maṇḍala-kīraṇa śatā-praseka-vyāsa-niśamana-mahāmudrā-sattva-varada svāhā.
The Root Mantra of the Great Body of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes.
